pk.context: 100 mg subcutaneous, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: clear, colorless to light yellow solution in a single-dose prefilled pen

tell: An IL-23 p19 antibody with only about 49% absolute bioavailability after a 100 mg subcutaneous injection.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability after a single subcutaneous injection is about 49%. It is expected to be broken down into small peptides and amino acids by ordinary catabolic pathways.
Made in a mammalian cell line by recombinant DNA technology, with a molecular weight of about 147 kilodaltons.
A BLA product in 100 mg/mL and 200 mg/2 mL single-dose pens and syringes, given at weeks 0 and 4 and then every 8 weeks.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated after serious hypersensitivity to the drug or its excipients; upper respiratory infections are among the reported reactions.
Plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis in adults and in children from 6 years of age weighing at least 40 kg, plus ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease in adults.
Selectively binds the p19 subunit of interleukin-23, inhibiting its interaction with the IL-23 receptor and the release of proinflammatory cytokines.
The generic name begins with G and has ten letters.
